text: Every company runs on knowledge scattered across documents, databases and spreadsheets. Finding an answer usually means finding the right person.
Vikram is a key account manager at Grand Line Shipping, a global container shipping company and EagleEye helps him find answers to business questions.
On Thursday he meets one of the company's largest customers, so he adds his recent meeting notes into the app.
A click on the file will display its contents, which EagleEye will use to search and cite information.
Alongside his notes sit hundreds of company documents, every policy and report, as well as the company's operations database.
Each document is processed the moment it is uploaded: its text, tables, and charts. All of it can be searched, and used in generating the response.
On request, EagleEye reads his notes, searches the company's policies, and queries the database, to generate an answer.
The brief is built around the topics in his own uploaded notes.
These claim counts come straight from a query on the operations database.
The alarm rules are quoted from the company's Reefer SOP, an enterprise document, with citations.
And the reliability comparison is a second database query, with context from a network review report.
And every citation opens the exact passage in the original document.
This answer was read from a chart. When the document was added, each chart was described in text, so the search can find it like any passage.
An SQL query is generated and executed to answer business questions, and the query is made available so anyone can check exactly how an answer was reached.
Vikram uploads a year of voyage data, and EagleEye profiles it at once: columns, gaps, correlations. Then he asks for a full exploratory analysis on Vessel Emissions.
Here is what happens behind the scenes. A safety check reads the request first, then the planner decides this needs a full notebook.
The analysis agent loads the file and writes the notebook: eight cells, from data quality through to comparisons by vessel class.
Now the notebook runs, as real Python, in an isolated sandbox with no network access. Five figures and seven tables come back from his data.
Finally, the findings are written from those results, and every number quoted is checked against the tables before the answer appears.
An afternoon of analyst work, ready in minutes.
Not every request is innocent. Sam, an intern, tries his luck.
Every message is screened before it reaches the model, and data access is enforced by role in the data layer itself, not in the prompt. HR data is simply out of Sam's reach.
EagleEye. Your company's knowledge, data and files, answered with evidence.
